band.name: Widespread Panic
band.blurb: Widespread Panic formed in Athens, Georgia in 1986 and is one of the longest-running American jam bands, turning 40 this year. On stage are John Bell, Dave Schools, JoJo Hermann, Sunny Ortiz and Duane Trucks, with Nick Johnson on lead guitar while Jimmy Herring is off the road for cancer treatment. The band has played a multi-night Milwaukee stand at the Riverside nearly every year since 2006, and Pabst Theater Group's CEO says the run has put Milwaukee 'in the pantheon of venues like Red Rocks.' These three sold-out nights are the last shows before the Halloween run in New Orleans, and Panic does not repeat a song across a run, so each night is its own setlist.

shows.notes: Night one. The free WOLPH street party on Wisconsin Ave outside the theater starts at 5:30 PM. After-party: Houseplant at Mo's Irish Pub (142 W Wisconsin Ave), 11:00 PM, right after the show.
Night two. Free WOLPH street party at 5:30 PM. After-party: Houseplant at Mo's Irish Pub, 11:00 PM.

Closing night, and the band's last show before the Oct 30-31 Halloween run in New Orleans. Free WOLPH street party at 5:30 PM. After-party: Armchair Boogie, a Madison bluegrass-jam quartet, at Mo's Irish Pub, 11:00 PM.

venue.name: Riverside Theater
venue.blurb: The Riverside is a 1928 French Baroque vaudeville palace on the west bank of the Milwaukee River, and Widespread Panic's unofficial Midwest home. I have only seen it in photographs, and in every one the balcony looks like it is leaning over the stage.

image.credit: Michael Barera / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 4.0

venue.history: RKO opened the Riverside on April 29, 1928 as a vaudeville-and-film house by Milwaukee architects Kirchhoff and Rose, who also drew up New York's Palace Theatre. The Three Stooges, Abbott and Costello, and a young Frank Sinatra with Tommy Dorsey all played here. A 1966 fire took out the ornate ceiling, the theater went dark in 1982, and philanthropist Joseph Zilber's $1.5 million restoration reopened it in 1984. Pabst Theater Group took over in 2005 and added a new marquee and 40-foot vertical sign in 2015-16. The original Wurlitzer organ still sits beneath the stage.
tips: Hey Baby, bag policy first: small purses only, 13"W x 4"D x 9"H or smaller, and they will be searched. Backpacks and oversized bags are turned away and there is no bag storage, so the big bag stays at the Drury.
Re-entry: the official FAQ does not address it, so plan as if there is none. Finish the street party and Mo's before you scan in.

Will call: the Riverside box office (116 W Wisconsin Ave) opens at 12:00 PM on event days, and will call opens 2 hours before showtime. Bring photo ID, and only the original purchaser can pick up. AXS mobile tickets live in the AXS app and cannot be printed.

Best entrance: the main doors under the marquee on W Wisconsin Ave, right at the river. Arrive at least 30 minutes before you want to be inside for security screening. The GA line for the pit forms early along Wisconsin Ave.
Money: bars and concessions are cashless (cards, Apple Pay, Google Pay), so no ATM hunt. Restroom locations are not published, so ask an usher.
Prohibited: outside food or drink (including water), vapes, laser pens, signs, flags, selfie sticks, tablets, pro cameras with zoom lenses, and any flash photography. Phone cameras are fine.
Merch: Pabst Theater Group runs an online store, and the in-venue tables are usually in the lobby. Run posters tend to sell out night one.
Parking is not your problem, you are walking. If a friend drives, the Gimbels Structure at 555 N Plankinton Ave takes Pabst advance parking passes.

hotel.name: Drury Plaza Hotel Milwaukee Downtown
hotel.blurb: The Drury sits inside the 1928 Art Deco First Financial Centre at Water and Wisconsin, directly across the river from the Riverside. The free 5:30 Kickback (hot appetizers and drinks) lines up with pre-show, and the free hot breakfast will do its part the morning after.
amenities: Connected to the Milwaukee skywalk system
hotel.building_history: Built in 1928 as the First Financial Centre, designed by Eschweiler & Eschweiler in Art Deco style; the 14-story tower's facade was bricked over in the 1980s and restored during Drury's two-year conversion.
hotel.resolution_note: The maps.app.goo.gl short link redirects to maps.google.com with q=Drury+Plaza+Hotel+Milwaukee+Downtown,+700+N+Water+St,+Milwaukee,+WI+53202.

walk.route_summary: Step out of the Drury onto N Water St at E Wisconsin Ave and turn west. Cross the Wisconsin Avenue Bridge over the Milwaukee River (the RiverWalk runs underneath on both banks), and the Riverside marquee is on your right on the far bank at 116 W Wisconsin Ave. Mo's Irish Pub, the after-party spot, is a few doors further west at 142 W Wisconsin. The whole walk is about 600 feet, and the theater's vertical sign is visible from the hotel door.

fan_tips: Hey Baby, the free WOLPH street party starts at 5:30 PM each night on Wisconsin Ave right outside the Riverside, same small-purse rules. Wolph is a young Grateful Dead-leaning jam band whose originals are being produced by Dave Schools, so expect the Panic crowd to actually watch.
Take the Drury's free 5:30 Kickback first, then cross the bridge for the street party. Two free happy hours in a row before an 8:00 PM show is the local move.

Panic does not repeat songs across consecutive shows, so fans trade setlist theories between nights. Pull up Everyday Companion or setlist.fm Saturday morning and you will have an opinion on what is 'due' by Sunday.

After the encore, the official after-parties are at Mo's Irish Pub (142 W Wisconsin Ave), a few doors west of the theater: Houseplant Friday and Saturday, Armchair Boogie Sunday, all at 11:00 PM. Tickets were sold as add-ons at Panic checkout, so check the AXS link if you did not grab one.

Locals call the neighborhood 'Milwookie' for this weekend. Nearly 10,000 fans from 48 states come in for the run, so the bars within a few blocks (Water St, Old World Third St) will be wall-to-wall tie-dye. Make dinner reservations early or eat before 5.
Riverside beer is reasonably priced and the bars are cashless. The GA pit line forms early on Wisconsin Ave, while 2nd-floor reserved seats mean you can wander in at 7:30 without stress.

Sunday is closing night and the band's last stop before Halloween in New Orleans, so expect a longer, looser show and a late night at Mo's. Your flight is not until about 3 PM Monday, so sleep in and still make the free breakfast.
